extracted.intended_audience: Prospective applicants to the NEH Public Scholars program (individual writers, independent researchers, scholars, and journalists seeking support to write a nonfiction humanities book for a broad public).
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for applying to the National Endowment for the Humanities Public Scholars program, which funds well-researched nonfiction humanities books for a general audience. Covers eligibility, application components, submission procedures, and administrative expectations for a 6–12 month book project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program purpose: well-researched nonfiction books for the broad public
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Scholars program supports the creation of well-researched nonfiction books in the humanities written for the broad public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program aims to strengthen the research underlying books and to encourage academic writers to communicate the significance of their research to the broadest possible range of readers. NEH especially encourages applications from independent writers, researchers, scholars, and journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: open to individuals; no advanced degree required
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers with or without an academic affiliation may apply, and no advanced degree is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program is intended both to encourage non-academic writers to deepen their engagement with the humanities and to encourage academic writers to communicate broadly. Special encouragement to independent writers who do not have a long-term position at an academic institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected output: book
rubrics_metrics.description: Expected output for supported projects is a book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should propose research, writing, travel, and other activities leading to publication of a nonfiction humanities book for a broad public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amount and period of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum award amount: $5,000 per month; Period of performance: six to twelve months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project start dates are indicated (e.g., September 1, 2022; September 1, 2023). Applicants should plan budgets and schedules consistent with the monthly award rate and the 6–12 month performance period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: The page limit for the narrative section of the application has been reduced from four pages to three pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the project narrative concise and focused to fit within the three-page limit; follow any formatting rules in the Notice of Funding Opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required one-page plan of work attachment
rubrics_metrics.description: A new required one-page attachment indicating your plan of work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This attachment must succinctly describe your timeline, milestones, and major research/writing activities. It is a required element of the application package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required form for project location(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: A new required form indicating the location(s) where you will carry out your plan of work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List and document the physical location(s) of your work (e.g., home office, research archives, travel sites) per the required form instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the Notice of Funding Opportunity and Grants.gov instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the instructions outlined in the Notice of Funding Opportunity and Grants.gov instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin by reading the Notice of Funding Opportunity to understand expectations and restrictions for projects and to prepare the most effective application. Use the provided NEH application package and any program resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants.gov registration and account maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Register for an account on Grants.gov; if already registered, make sure it is up to date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register as soon as you know you're ready to apply. Use Grants.gov Applicant Tools and Tips. Failure to register or to keep account information current can prevent successful submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDF preparation (software and tips)
rubrics_metrics.description: Download Adobe Reader and follow Tips for making PDFs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare application components as PDFs according to Grants.gov and NEH guidance to avoid formatting or submission errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission and confirmation via Grants.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit your application package on Grants.gov; you will receive a confirmation from Grants.gov when you've successfully submitted your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After submission, Grants.gov will send up to five e-mail messages confirming receipt and different stages in acceptance. Verify that you have received all confirmation messages and check spam/junk folders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of reference: timing and applicant responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH requests letters of reference from your recommenders approximately seven to ten days after the application deadline. You will be notified by e-mail when each letter has been received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After receiving the fifth Grants.gov confirmation message (confirming NEH received your application), check the status of letters by logging in to NEH's secure area with your application and Grants.gov tracking numbers. You may send reminders (including the upload link) to letter writers from this site. Applicants are responsible for ensuring letter writers received solicitations and submitted their letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use program resources and models (sample narratives, funded projects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Program resources include Public Scholar Frequently Asked Questions, a list of recently funded projects, and Sample Application Narratives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review sample application narratives and examples of funded projects to understand successful proposals and the scope/scale of previously supported books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor application status and communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify you have received email messages from Grants.gov and monitor the status of submission and letters of recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for up to five confirmation emails from Grants.gov at different stages; verify they are received and follow up if not. Use NEH's secure site to monitor letter status after the fifth confirmation message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand program competitiveness and typical award statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Program statistics: NEH received an average of 278 applications per year; funding ratio ~9%; NEH made an average of 24 awards per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize competitiveness when crafting proposal and budget; use statistics to set realistic expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend or review information session for application guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: An information session explained the goals of the Public Scholars program, eligibility requirements, how to apply, how applications are reviewed, and how to write an effective application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch the recorded information session (closed captioning and transcript available) to learn about reviewers' expectations and tips for writing an effective application. An additional online session will be announced before future deadlines.
